messages:
alex: Heads up — us-west1 GPU attach failing since ~12:03 UTC, scheduler showing a bunch of nodes in 'disk_unhealthy' (nvme health-checker).

mira: seeing the same. GPU queue backlog up ~2.3x. Any SMART alerts popping?

ops-bot: nvme-health-checker: gnw-42 marked quarantine. Reason: per-namespace SMART wear_percent divergence > 300%.

samir: huh. wear_percent divergence across namespaces on the same device? can you paste a sample?

alex: ```json
{"node":"gnw-42","device":"nvme0n1","namespaces":[{"id":1,"wear":12.1},{"id":2,"wear":2.9},{"id":3,"wear":3.0}],"fw":"2.3.7"}
```

diane: 2.3.7? we rolled 2.3.7 to a few pools last week. there was a telemetry bug in older fw notes but I thought it was fixed.

mira: hypothesis: firmware telemetry bug is spuriously reporting one namespace at 12% while others are ~3% -> health-checker triggers quarantine -> GPUs can't attach to those hosts.

samir: can we validate by reading raw SMART counters / nvme-cli on an impacted host? alex, can you grab one?

alex: ran nvme-cli dump: `nvme smart-log --namespace-id=1 /dev/nvme0n1` shows high wear, but SMART raw bytes look inconsistent across ns.

alex: quick experiment: bumped health-checker per-ns tolerance to 20% on a single canary node in the pool — attach succeeded, backlog drained.

diane: good temporary proof. Options: 1) rollback fw on affected pool 2) patch health-checker to ignore per-namespace spikes when fw==2.3.7 3) add a telemetry sanity check to detect fw-caused skew.

samir: implement #2 first (faster), but we need an ops ticket to roll fw back across us-west1 canaries and then the fleet if rollback is safe. Also call out customer impact & cost.

mira: cost note: Dedicated capacity queues held for ~30m = estimate ~$1.2k of delayed throughput if it hits peak — CS needs a heads up.

cs-oncall: acknowledged. I'll send the templated incident notice to affected tenants in us-west1 and attach the mitigation steps.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/nvme-smart-mismatch (runbook: tolerance bump, telemetry dump, fw-rollback checklist).

alex: mitigation applied: health-checker tolerance bump + lowered scrub intensity from 0.8 -> 0.4 on affected pool. GPU attach resumed across the pool; backlog cleared.

samir: creating follow-up: INFRA-4521 (fw-rollback + add fw exceptions in health-checker + alerting for smart-skew). Assigning to @diane and @infra-teams.

diane: filing the rollback ticket now. will coordinate canary window and revert plan.

alex: leaving a short postmortem stub in docs, linking from the ticket. provisional mitigation looks stable, but we should watch for recurrence.

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated. Alerting suppressed for 24h. Reopen if smart-skew > 20% again.

mira: nice triage everyone. follow-ups: add a metric 'nvme.smart.skew' and a grafana panel. :rocket:
